agent.name: Emerging Technology Diffusion Agent
agent.specialty: Rogers diffusion evidence, application and peer scope, bounded organizational timing

analytical_question: How far have the defined technology and chart-review application diffused, what most accelerates or inhibits spread, and what timing implication follows for this organization without making the final adoption decision?
general_et_finding: NOT EVALUABLE FOR THE SPECIFIED UNIT. AI is not defined well enough to distinguish a chatbot, plugin or integrated agentic system. The source packet describes different units; withhold one combined diffusion stage or rate and request a system boundary.
application_finding: The proposed chart-review task is clear, but its enabling technology is ambiguous. Assess relative advantage, compatibility, complexity, trialability and observability only as questions until the system and peer population are specified; do not transfer the broad any-AI rate or agent statistic to the unnamed unit.
organization_specific_finding: The finance firm still requires permitted data and accountable release. Resolve the technology, comparator and peer population before diffusion-based timing; an aggressive label would not resolve the missing unit.

evidence.claim: Rogers five perceived attributes, adopter categories, decision stages, channels and chasm heuristic.
evidence.source_or_reference: S0 /Users/cyf/Documents/NYU/2026fall/1800/Slides/ET Module 6 - The Diffusion of Emerging Technologies FA25.pptx
evidence.date_or_recency: FA25 file supplied for this course; inspected 2026-10-26; checked 2026-10-26
evidence.notes: Conceptual lens, not observed agentic deployment. The 16% and messaging heuristics do not prove an empirical market threshold or irreversible diffusion.

evidence.claim: 40% of respondents at organizations with revenue above USD1 billion report scaling agents in one or more functions; 22% at smaller organizations. Survey: 1,719 participants, 97 nations, national GDP response weighting.
evidence.notes: Respondent self-report, not a probability estimate for every firm. One or more functions is not enterprise-wide scaling; neither is chart-review use or a finance-peer diffusion denominator. Fieldwork is not October 2026 deployment. No S-curve is fitted.

evidence.claim: For the period ending May 3, 2026, any-AI use was 33.9% in Finance and Insurance and 19.8% nationally; the core question asks about use in the past two weeks in any business function.
evidence.notes: US employer-business any-AI measure, not integrated agentic systems or chart-review deployment. The revised November 2025 wording prevents a naive continuous comparison with earlier production-only questions. Expectations are not observed future use. This is a dated comparison, not the latest October release.

evidence.claim: MCP became a founding project of the Linux Foundation Agentic AI Foundation, providing a concrete interoperability and governance ecosystem signal.
evidence.notes: Protocol availability and governance do not establish market penetration, safe integration, actual local use or chart-review effectiveness. Download/server counts are deliberately not used as adoption denominators.

contrary_evidence_or_limitations: A global enterprise self-report, a US any-AI firm measure and protocol availability use different units and cannot be averaged into one diffusion rate.
Some large enterprises may already have sustained scaling; this prevents treating all agentic systems as mere experiments, but supplies no direct chart-review peer count.
All companies, permissions and workflow roles here are teaching premises; no chart tool, pilot, causal diffusion experiment or realized business gain is demonstrated.
confidence_and_uncertainty: High confidence in the unit mismatch; current diffusion of the unspecified unit is not evaluable.
value_opportunity_implication: A transferable learning advantage is possible if source-linked correctness and full review effort improve against manual and simpler deterministic checks. Ecosystem complements may reduce integration friction, but this mechanism is inference, not measured local ROI.
risk_governance_implication: Popularity and social proof cannot authorize data access or publication. Maintain read-only boundaries and a named human report owner. Protocol availability does not certify a connector; unsuccessful trials or excessive review burden can justify stopping.
recommendation_management_implication: Request the usable system boundary and a matching source population, then reassess diffusion. Do not recommend rollout or manufacture a market category.
change_monitoring_triggers: A proposed reporting owner obtains dated, comparable evidence of the exact workflow in similar firms, with population, geography, use definition and repeat-use status.
An authorized owner supplies quality-adjusted comparison results including review, correction, connector and exception costs; worsening errors or maintenance burden can delay or end work.
Data-environment permission or support capacity changes; reassess at the end of the four-week evidence window and within the twelve-month horizon, without a promised takeoff date.
abstention_or_more_information_needed: Request a defined peer denominator and comparable repeated chart-review deployments before assigning penetration or a majority/chasm label.
Request a local comparator and approved environment before making claims about realized advantage or internal rollout timing.
